title: Interim SKY staking rewards are funded from buybacks and reserves through a vesting stream, not from emissions
content:
A.4.4.1.4 frames the whole subsection as temporary: it defines "short-term SKY staking rewards pending the full implementation of the Sky Treasury Management Function," and A.4.4.1.4.2 confirms the sunset — "this interim mechanism will be discontinued once the USDS Staking Rewards become operational."

The funding constraint is the load-bearing part. A.4.4.1.4.2.2 states that "the `vestTot` and `vestTau` parameters of the Vesting Stream contract are set such that SKY rewards are funded by SKY acquired through buybacks or SKY reserves." The no-new-emissions rule is thus honoured even by a stopgap: rewards are paid from tokens the protocol already bought or holds, and the vesting parameters are the enforcement point rather than a separate policy statement.

The implementation is a three-contract chain (A.4.4.1.4.2.1): a Vesting Stream that releases SKY from the Protocol Treasury, a Rewards Distribution contract that forwards it, and a user-facing Staking Rewards contract that accrues per-user balances against `LSSKY` as the staking token. Rate control happens by adjusting the vesting stream — A.4.4.1.4.2.1.3.3 lets the Core Facilitator, consulting the Risk Advisor, modify `vestTot`/`vestTau` "to achieve the target reward rate" directly via Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll.

That is the elegant part: because a linear vesting stream is a rate, the reward APY becomes a function of two numbers in one contract, and no new distribution logic is needed to change it. The transitional design also stays deliberately compatible with the end state — same user contract, same staking token — so retiring it means redirecting a funding source, not migrating users.
